raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Identity" },
  "read": "This student did everything right — they studied — and still came up short, which is the most demoralizing kind of failure. They are not being lazy; they are trying to protect their self-worth by explaining the gap as fixed ability rather than a skill they haven't cracked yet. The identity piece shows up because 'I'm just bad at this' is becoming a story they tell about who they are.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Rushing to say 'it's okay, you tried your best' — which sounds kind but quietly confirms that trying hard and still failing might mean they really can't do it." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the expectation that they will keep working at this material, while naming the effort as evidence of capability and reframing the poor result as a signal about strategy, not about ceiling.",
  "holdFirm": ["You are going to keep working at this — one result does not close the door.", "We are going to figure out what the studying missed, not whether studying is worth doing."],
  "stayFlexible": ["How they review, what they review, and who they work with are all on the table.", "Let them name what felt confusing versus what felt clear — their own diagnosis builds buy-in."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey — I saw you on this. I know you put time in, and I want to talk about that for a second because it matters." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When you were studying, what did that actually look like? Walk me through it — because I want to understand what happened, not just look at the score." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I think is going on: the effort was real, but the method and the test were not speaking the same language yet. That is a strategy problem, and strategy is something we can actually change. Can we look at two or three questions together and figure out where the gap opened up?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to keeping at this — not because I enjoy it when things are hard, but because I have high standards for you and I genuinely believe you can get there. A brain that studied and came up short is a brain that is still building the skill, not one that hit its limit." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time this student gets a little further with revised strategies and sees improvement, the fixed-ability story loses ground — point that out explicitly when it happens, so they start to see effort and method as the actual levers."
}
situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.
